newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan industrial output on upward trend -- MITI.
newsitem.headline: Japan industrial output on upward trend -- MITI.

text.p: Japan's industrial production is on an upward trend, an official from the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) told a news conference on Wednesday.
The official, briefing reporters on data for December, said the improvement was based on expectations that production would continue to maintain high levels and inventories would also keep improving.
The ministry dropped from its monthly assessment of the upward trend the word "gradual", which it had used since February last year.
The official also said that taking into account movements of both production and inventories over the last few months, the improvement trend was clear.
He said that based on the ministry's forecasts, the improvement in production was likely to continue in the near term.

Asked whether MITI expected the rise in production to continue beyond April, when the government plans to raise the consumption tax to five percent from three percent, he said the forecast only covered up to the end of February.

According to MITI's forecast, output for manufacturers is expected to rise 5.4 percent in January but to fall 2.9 percent in February. The official said the drop in the February forecast was largely due to the strong January figure.
He said inventories were decreasing due to strong demand.

Asked whether the yen's weakening had any effect on industrial production, the official said companies were likely to have drawn up their plans for January and February taking into account the yen's recent weakness.
